title: Pancake Flipping
strapline: Whisk the batter, watch it bubble, and hold your breath for the big flip.
intent: Children take part in a quick, exciting cooking process with a thrilling moment at its heart.
Children measure and count ingredients and pour, whisk and mix with control.
Children observe change — runny batter turns golden and firm in the pan.
Children explore early sharing and fractions as pancakes are cut and topped.
Children build coordination, courage and anticipation around the flip.
implementation: Whisk a simple batter together, counting and measuring the ingredients as you go.
Let children pour, whisk and mix, coaching control and taking turns with the bowl.
Talk through the change: 'it's runny now — watch what the heat does', bubbles then golden.
Do the flipping safely at an adult-led pan, with children counting down and cheering it over.
Cut and share the pancakes and offer toppings — halves and quarters, one topping each, fair shares.
Build the anticipation and language — 'ready, steady, FLIP!' — and celebrate the wobbly ones too.
Talk about Pancake Day and the different pancakes families make around the world.
key_questions: How does the batter change when it hits the hot pan?
How many spoons of flour shall we count in?
Ready, steady — shall we count down to the flip?
How can we cut the pancake so two people share it fairly?
What topping would you choose, and how many?

impact.text: Children take part in a whole cooking process from batter to plate.
Children measure and count ingredients and pour, whisk and mix with control.
Children observe and talk about change as batter cooks to golden pancake.
Children cut and share pancakes into halves and quarters and count toppings.
Children build anticipation and courage around the flip and cheer each other on.
Children connect pancakes to Pancake Day and pancakes made around the world.

enhancements: A simple batter recipe with picture steps.
Whisks, bowls, jugs and measuring spoons.
An adult-led pan and a child-height view of the cooking.
Toppings to choose and count — lemon, berries, banana.
Plates and blunt knives for cutting and fair sharing.
A countdown chart for the big flip.
Pictures of pancakes from different countries and kitchens.

playing_exploring: Children explore the batter — pouring, whisking, watching it drip and bubble.
They test how much to pour and what each topping tastes like.
active_learning: The flip is a shared, exciting goal everyone counts towards.
Children take turns whisking the stiff batter, putting in real effort.
creating_thinking: Children predict what the heat will do and watch to check.
They solve fair sharing and choose how to top their own pancake.
